claims.text: Machine learning-based interatomic potentials can be used to produce three-dimensional NM-HEA nanoframeworks.
Machine learning-based interatomic potentials can simulate NM-HEA formation.
Machine learning-based interatomic potentials can optimize NM-HEA structures.
NM-HEAs have diverse compositions and complex surface structures.
Applying machine learning-based interatomic potentials produces an optimized NM-HEA structure with controlled atomic arrangement.
DFT simulations can predict NM-HEA behavior at the atomic level.
MD simulations can predict NM-HEA behavior at the atomic level.
Structure optimization will improve precise atomic control in NM-HEAs.
The proposed simulations will improve understanding of NM-HEA formation mechanisms.
Improved atomic control and understanding of formation mechanisms will lead to production of three-dimensional NM-HEA nanoframeworks.
The relevant catalytic conditions may include high temperatures, pressures, and reactive environments.
Computational-resource limitations constrain the proposed method.
The accuracy of machine learning models constrains the proposed method.
There is uncertainty in transferring simulated NM-HEA structures to experimental conditions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes interatomic potentials as directly producing nanoframeworks, while the stated intervention is computational simulation and optimization. No physical synthesis step is specified, yet the experiment refers to structures produced using the potentials.
